content: 1. Both lamivudine and nevirapine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Similarly, nevirapine and tenofovir DF also elevate this risk. Close monitoring is advised when these drugs are used. 2. Tenofovir DF reduces the levels of nintedanib through the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration with P-gp inducers, especially those that are also CYP3A4 inducers, should be avoided or alternative drugs should be considered. Nintedanib is a substrate of P-gp and, to a lesser extent, CYP3A4. 3. Orlistat decreases the levels and effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly, possibly due to a drug-drug interaction that inhibits systemic absorption of the antiretroviral drug. Frequent monitoring of HIV RNA levels is recommended, and orlistat should be discontinued if an increased viral load is confirmed. 4. Oteseconazole, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the effects and toxicities of BCRP substrates, including tenofovir DF. Therapy modification or close monitoring is necessary, and the lowest starting dose of the BCRP substrate should be used. 5. Oxaliplatin and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. This combination may also elevate tenofovir levels. Caution and close monitoring are required. 6. Co-administration of tenofovir DF with oxaprozin increases the levels of both drugs by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised to prevent potential toxicity. 7. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels and effects of doravirine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine. 8. Pamidronate increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance, which may heighten the risk of nephrotoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 9. Paromomycin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Paromomycin also raises tenofovir levels by decreasing elimination. Close monitoring is advised. 10. Peginterferon alfa-2a or alfa-2b, when combined with lamivudine, increases the risk of liver decompensation due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 11. Pemetrexed and tenofovir DF increase each other’s levels by reducing renal clearance, leading to potential nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are required. 12. Penicillamine and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Penicillamine also raises tenofovir levels by reducing renal clearance. Close monitoring is advised. 13. Pentamidine and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. This combination may also elevate tenofovir levels. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 14. Pentobarbital decreases the levels and effects of doravirine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 15. Peramivir levels are increased by tenofovir DF due to reduced renal clearance. Caution is advised when peramivir is co-administered with nephrotoxic drugs. 16. Phenobarbital decreases doravirine levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 17. Phenytoin reduces doravirine levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated for the same reasons as above. 18. Piroxicam and tenofovir DF increase each other’s levels by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to toxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 19. Posaconazole increases doravirine levels and effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary to avoid toxicity. 20. Pramipexole levels are increased by tenofovir DF due to reduced renal clearance, which may lead to toxicity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 21. Probenecid increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to toxicity. Close monitoring is recommended. 22. Procainamide levels are elevated by tenofovir DF due to reduced renal clearance, increasing the risk of toxicity. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 23. Quinidine and tenofovir DF increase each other’s levels by reducing renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 24. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 25. Ribavirin increases lamivudine toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of lactic acidosis. Alternatives should be considered if available. 26. Rifabutin decreases doravirine levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administered, the doravirine dose should be increased to 100 mg twice daily during rifabutin therapy. 27. Rifampin reduces doravirine levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 28. Ritonavir increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination and raises the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome when combined with lamivudine or tenofovir DF. Close monitoring is necessary. 29. Safinamide and its metabolite may inhibit intestinal BCRP, increasing the effects and adverse reactions of BCRP substrates like tenofovir DF. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 30. Alternative drugs should be considered. 31. St. John’s Wort decreases doravirine levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 32. Stiripentol inhibits BCRP transport and increases tenofovir DF levels and effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 33. Streptomycin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Streptomycin also raises tenofovir levels by reducing elimination. Caution and close monitoring are required. 34. Streptozocin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. This combination is contraindicated due to the high risk of toxicity. 35. Sulfamethoxazole increases lamivudine levels by reducing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 36. Tacrolimus and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 37. Dosage adjustments may be required, and close monitoring is advised. 38. Tafenogquine inhibits OCT2 and MATE transporters, increasing lamivudine levels. Co-administration should be avoided, or close monitoring and dosage adjustments should be implemented. 39. Telavancin increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance, heightening the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 40. Tenofovir DF and zidovudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Lamivudine enhances zidovudine effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, which may be beneficial. 41. HIV-infected women are advised not to breastfeed due to the risk of postnatal HIV transmission. 42. Doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir DF are antiretroviral agents with specific mechanisms of action targeting HIV replication. They are part of a complete regimen for adults without prior antiretroviral therapy history. These medications should not be combined with other antiretroviral drugs. 43. Patients should take these medications at a consistent time daily, with or without food. Store them at 20–25°C (68–77°F) in their original, tightly closed bottles to protect from moisture.
